problem:
Which of the following sets are finite?

- $P({Z,t,n})$
- $P(Z)$
- $P({{2}^{n}∣n\in Z})$
worked_solution:
The power set of a finite set is finite, while the power set of an infinite set is infinite.

With that in mind, let's examine our sets.

- Set I is finite since the underlying set is finite. Notice that 

$$
P({Z,t,n})={∅,\,{Z},\,{t},\,{n},\,{Z,t},{Z,n},\,{t,n},\,{Z,t,n}}
$$

has cardinality $8.$

- Set II is infinite since the underlying set $Z$ is infinite.

- Set III is infinite since the underlying set ${{2}^{n}∣n\in Z}$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
